steps.title: Design and subclone GFP‑aequorin‑opt
steps.instruction: Generate a codon‑optimized GFP‑aequorin sequence (aequorin‑opt) for zebrafish using the IDT online codon‑optimization tool, then subclone the optimized gene into a PT2 14xUAS plasmid.

steps.title: Prepare injection mix and inject embryos
steps.instruction: Mix 2 µl ADN (120 ng/µl) + 2 µl ARN transposase (175 ng/µl) + 1 µl 2 M KCl + 1 µl 2 % phenol red, then bring the volume to 10 µl with Milli‑Q H₂O; inject this solution into Tg(mnx1:gal4) icm11 embryos to generate Tg(mnx1:gal4;UAS:GFP‑aequorin‑opt) icm09 double‑transgenic larvae.

steps.title: Maintain fish and raise embryos in blue water
steps.instruction: Keep adult AB and Tüpfel long‑fin (TL) zebrafish on a 14 h light/10 h dark cycle at 28.5 °C, conductivity 500 µS, pH 7.4. Raise injected embryos in “blue water” (3 g Instant Ocean® salts + 2 ml 1 % methylene blue per 10 L ultrapure water) at 28.5 °C for the first 24 h before screening for GFP expression.

steps.title: Fix and immunostain larvae
steps.instruction: Fix 4 dpf larvae in 4 % PFA for 4 h at 4 °C, then wash 3 × 5 min in PBS. Block 1 h in blocking solution (10 % NGS, 1 % DMSO, 0.5 % Triton X‑100 in 0.1 M PBS) with agitation. Incubate overnight at 4 °C with primary anti‑GFP antibody (1:500) in incubation solution (1 % NGS, 1 % DMSO, 0.5 % Triton X‑100 in 0.1 % PBS) with agitation. Wash 3 × 5 min in washing solution (0.1 M PBST with 0.5 % Triton X‑100). Incubate 2 h at room temperature in the dark with secondary Alexa Fluor 488 goat anti‑chicken IgG (1:1000) in PBST with agitation. Wash 3 × 5 min in PBST, mount larvae with Vector H‑1000 mounting medium, and image on an Olympus FV‑1000 confocal microscope. Perform negative controls by omitting the primary antibody.

steps.title: Prepare coelenterazine‑h stock solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve lyophilized coelenterazine‑h to make a 10 mM stock (e.g., 250 µg, M = 407.5 g mol⁻¹, final volume 60 µl). Add propylene glycol to 25 % of the final volume (≈15.4 µl). Sonicate cyclodextrin at 45 % (4.5 g in 10 ml) and add it to 75 % of the final volume (≈46 µl).

steps.title: Soak embryos in coelenterazine solution
steps.instruction: De‑chorionate embryos at 1 day post‑fertilization under a microscope. Prepare a 60 µM soaking solution by diluting the 10 mM stock in blue water (e.g., 6 µl stock in 1 ml for 10 embryos). Place each de‑chorionated embryo in 100 µl of this solution in a sealed 48‑well plate and incubate overnight at 26 °C in the dark. Renew the soaking solution at 2 dpf and keep embryos in the dark until 4 dpf (total soaking time 72 h).

steps.title: Assemble lightproof bioluminescence apparatus
steps.instruction: Construct a 1 m × 1 m light‑proof box using black boards. Install an 850 nm LED with two long‑pass filters (780 nm and 810 nm) and a diffuser for infrared illumination. Set up a high‑speed infrared‑sensitive camera (1000 Hz, 320 × 320 px) controlled by Hiris® software. Position a photomultiplier tube (PMT) beneath the larval arena, connected to an acquisition card. Place a 525 nm ± 25 nm band‑pass filter and a 670 nm short‑pass filter between the larva and the PMT. Use a custom API to synchronize video, photon counting, and stimulus delivery via a 30‑trial TTL sequence.

steps.title: Conduct bioluminescence assay on individual larvae
steps.instruction: Place a single 4 dpf larva in a circular 3D‑printed arena (2 cm diameter) or head‑embed in 1.5 % low‑melting‑point agarose with the tail free. Attach the arena to a 2‑Ω speaker. Deliver sinusoidal acoustic stimuli (5 cycles at 500 Hz) via a waveform generator and audio amplifier; set stimulus intensity to the lowest voltage that reliably elicits an escape (typically 0.5–5 V). For each trial, record 500 ms baseline, deliver a 10 ms stimulus, then record for 1990 ms. Perform 30 trials with 1‑min inter‑trial intervals to reduce habituation.
